new_findings.name: Shelf-space estimation
new_findings.explanation: The system must design an estimation algorithm to track shelf space, considering various methods like item dimensions or counts as proxies. This is necessary due to the absence of direct tracking in the database.

new_findings.name: Auto-Revert Policy Specification
new_findings.explanation: Details around the time period for auto-reverting transferred items and which events might trigger immediate reversion should be clearly defined, ensuring that the policy can be effectively implemented.

new_findings.name: Retention and transaction-history window
new_findings.explanation: The project currently lacks clarity on the default time frame for retaining transaction history, which must be configurable and agreed upon by stakeholders to ensure compliance with reporting needs.

new_findings.name: Query History Tracking per Item
new_findings.explanation: The system should provide a mechanism to track and display the history of queries made by staff on individual items, which helps in maintaining the transparency of data access and operations. Additionally, understanding the history of queries can aid in identifying common search patterns and optimization areas.

new_findings.name: Resource Consumption Monitoring
new_findings.explanation: The system must incorporate a feature to monitor and log resource consumption by queries and report executions, allowing for an analysis of performance impacts across branches. Understanding resource utilization will be essential for optimization and troubleshooting.

new_findings.name: Health Monitoring Functionality
new_findings.explanation: The system should include built-in health monitoring features that provide status updates regarding system performance, uptime, and any flagged issues. This ensures proactive management and quick responses to potential problems.

new_findings.name: Communication of System Updates
new_findings.explanation: There should be a structured means to communicate updates or outages to users effectively. This could include a notification system that alerts staff of updates and any expected downtime as well as major changes to reporting functionality.

new_findings.name: Configurable User Preference Settings
new_findings.explanation: The system must offer user-configurable settings that allow staff to define their preferences for report formatting, visibility options, and notification settings, to improve usability and user satisfaction.

new_findings.name: Accessibility Compliance Update
new_findings.explanation: The requirements specify compliance with Section 508 and older browsers without confirmation on whether these legacy versions remain required or if the policy will be updated.

new_findings.name: Additional Report Types Needed
new_findings.explanation: The requirements highlight missing report types related to circulation and collection analysis such as circulation count by Dewey or MARC fields, which are necessary for a complete analytical capability.

new_findings.name: Operational Separation from OPAC
new_findings.explanation: The reporting system should not affect the performance of the OPAC module to prevent slowdowns for library patrons.

new_findings.name: Help System Navigation and Accessibility
new_findings.explanation: The online help system should be hierarchical, cross-linked, searchable, and easy to navigate. This is critical for usability and support.

new_findings.name: Reports Interface Specification Adaptation
new_findings.explanation: The project intends to adapt an existing Software Requirements Specification (SRS) developed by Galecia Group for specific PINES needs, suggesting additional insights are required on adaptation processes.

new_findings.name: Missing Report Types for Circulation and Collection Analysis
new_findings.explanation: The current system lacks several report types related to circulation and collection analysis, such as circulation count by Dewey or MARC fields, age of collection by call number, and fines stopped reasons. Expanding report types to include these will enhance analytical capabilities.

new_findings.name: Advanced Scheduling and Delivery Options
new_findings.explanation: The reporting system lacks options for scheduling reports at granular frequencies like hourly, daily, weekly, monthly, or yearly, and does not support email delivery or address book-based report distribution.

new_findings.name: Report Queue Visibility and Management
new_findings.explanation: The system currently does not support visibility into report queues, prioritization, or cancellation of running reports, which are essential features for effective report management.

new_findings.name: Rich Output Formats and Customization
new_findings.explanation: The current report output formats are limited to CSV, HTML, and sometimes Excel, without support for pivot tables or advanced formatting. Additionally, there's no capability for report template management or editing display options.

The system should count and track record deletions (e.g., item records,
patron records) per location and per system.

new_findings.name: Query History Tracking

new_findings.explanation: The system should generate consolidated reports that aggregate item statuses for all items (not just missing or damaged), allowing for a clearer overview of collection health and operational needs across the branches.

new_findings.name: Replication Health Monitoring Functions
new_findings.explanation: The reporting system should include monitoring functions to track the health of data replication between the primary database and reporting environments, ensuring integrity and synchrony in reporting data.

new_findings.name: Data Ownership and Retention Policies Documentation

new_findings.name: Reports Interface Software Requirements Specification Adaptation
new_findings.explanation: The group intends to adapt the existing Software Requirements Specification (SRS) developed by Galecia Group for King County Library System, to suit PINES-specific needs for a reports interface. This adaptive process involves reviewing the draft shared by Galecia Group and tailoring it for PINES requirements.

new_findings.name: Functional Requirements for Reports and Management Processes
new_findings.explanation: The system must efficiently support reporting and analysis functions used by library managers, administrators, and staff for planning, evaluation, and oversight. These functions are explicitly scoped to management processes and do not include patron-facing OPAC or circulation functions.

new_findings.name: Report Development and Testing Responsibilities
new_findings.explanation: The Reports Working Group is tasked with documenting optimal Reports functionality within a future Evergreen release, developing a list of requirements, and becoming the designated testing group to evaluate all new Reports development.

new_findings.name: Report Templates Specification for PINES Libraries
new_findings.explanation: The system should include the capability to determine and create standardized report templates needed across PINES member libraries, facilitating consistent reporting and potential customization.

new_findings.name: User Interface Focus on Functional Requirements
new_findings.explanation: The current focus for system specification is on functional requirements, with the understanding that user interface (UI) details and data structures will be developed iteratively using a prototype-oriented methodology.

new_findings.name: Management Process Data Scope Definition
new_findings.explanation: The system must support analysis of the library collection, branch capacity, demographics, staff productivity, and financial transactions, specifically for management activities and decision-making, excluding patron-facing functionalities.

new_findings.name: Development Approach and Documentation Readability Goals
new_findings.explanation: The requirements documentation should be written in a manner accessible to both technical and non-technical stakeholders, emphasizing readability for non-technical audiences while providing sufficient detail for developers. The development process will be iterative and collaborative, incorporating user feedback through prototypes.

new_findings.name: Action Items for Requirement Gathering and Review Schedule
new_findings.explanation: Members will conduct interviews to gather report needs, Katherine will circulate draft requirements, and follow-up meetings will review findings. This process is scheduled with a deadline of April 15, 2009, for interviews, with subsequent review in July 2009.

new_findings.explanation: The system must include functionality to generate reports identifying items that were deleted and were the last copies in the facility to support proper data maintenance with external catalogs like WorldCat.

new_findings.name: Electronic Activity Reporting for Patrons
new_findings.explanation: The system must ensure electronic activities such as OPAC logins and online renewals are included in inactivity reporting to maintain comprehensive patron engagement metrics.

new_findings.name: Inactivity Threshold Customization
new_findings.explanation: The inactivity threshold should be configurable by the user, allowing flexibility in targeting patrons based on customized periods of inactivity.

new_findings.name: Authentication Options and Individual Auditability
new_findings.explanation: The system shall support multiple staff login methods including streamlined local login (e.g., card-swipe) and traditional username/password. Streamlined login shall still identify the specific staff member for audit purposes, and role-based access control shall be used so that changing a user's role updates their permissions automatically.

new_findings.name: Permissions and Role Restrictions for Transfer & Report Actions
new_findings.explanation: The system shall restrict transfer, purge, and other data-modifying functions to authorized roles (e.g., managers, administrators, transfer coordinators).

new_findings.name: Development / Training Environments and Configuration Migration
new_findings.explanation: The system shall provide separate development/training environments where reports and configurations may be developed and tested without affecting production. new_findings.name: Electronic activity inclusion for inactivity reports
new_findings.explanation: The report must include electronic activity metrics such as OPAC login, online hold placement, renewing online, and digital collection access, to identify patrons active electronically but not physically. The necessity for this inclusion is a critical operational requirement, as stated by multiple stakeholders for comprehensive inactivity reporting.

new_findings.name: Inclusion of current mailing addresses in report for outreach
new_findings.explanation: The report must include current mailing addresses of patrons to facilitate outreach efforts like mailing postcards, which is necessary for direct engagement with inactive patrons for reactivation.

new_findings.name: Data Quality Documentation Requirement
new_findings.explanation: The system shall include a requirement to document data quality constraints and issues when specifying item records and libraries for reporting.

new_findings.name: Logging of Transfer Activities
new_findings.explanation: All transfer actions, including batch updates, manual transfers, and reverts, should be logged for audit and tracking purposes.

new_findings.name: Support for Time-Based and Event-Based Auto Revert
new_findings.explanation: The auto-revert feature should handle both elapsed time (e.g., 30 days) and specific events, like status change to 'sold' or item being checked out at a destination.

new_findings.name: Automatic Reversion after Transfer Period
new_findings.explanation: The utility must support reversion of transferred items to their original location automatically after a specified time or triggered by certain criteria, such as status changes or checkouts.

new_findings.name: Transfer Delay Alerts and Notifications
new_findings.explanation: The system should notify users if an item transfer is delayed or encounters issues. This entails alerts or notification mechanisms.

new_findings.name: Transfer Activity Logging and Item Transfer History
new_findings.explanation: All transfer-related activities (batch updates, manual transfers, reverts, pull-list generation, and notifications) shall be logged. The system shall allow viewing the transfer history for an individual item (for example, number of transfers in the past year) to identify circulation or location issues.

new_findings.name: Permissions and Role Restrictions for Transfer & Report Actions
new_findings.explanation: The system shall restrict transfer, purge, and other data-modifying functions to authorized roles (e.g., managers, administrators, transfer coordinators). Permissions shall be manageable via roles and security groups so that altering a user's role updates their permissions automatically.

new_findings.name: Help System and Error Reporting
new_findings.explanation: The system shall provide an integrated online help system in HTML that is hierarchical, cross-linked, searchable, and illustrates all major functions. The system shall also provide high-level error reporting and low-level query-specific feedback for administrators to support troubleshooting.

new_findings.name: Report Queue Visibility and Management
new_findings.explanation: The system does not currently support visibility into report queues, prioritization, or cancellation of running reports, which are essential features for effective report management.

new_findings.explanation: The system shall investigate methods to estimate shelf space from existing data (e.g., item dimensions or count as a proxy) due to the lack of direct tracking in the database. new_findings.name: Auto-Revert policy specifics

new_findings.name: Retention and transaction-history window
new_findings.explanation: The project currently lacks clarity on the default time frame for retaining transaction history, which must be configurable and agreed upon by stakeholders to ensure compliance with reporting needs.

new_findings.name: Query history tracking per item
new_findings.explanation: The system should provide a mechanism to track and display the history of queries made by staff on individual items, which helps in maintaining the transparency of data access and operations. Additionally, understanding the history of queries can aid in identifying common search patterns and optimization areas.

new_findings.name: Resource consumption monitoring
new_findings.explanation: The system must incorporate a feature to monitor and log resource consumption by queries and report executions, allowing for an analysis of performance impacts across branches. Understanding resource utilization will be essential for optimization and troubleshooting.

new_findings.name: Health monitoring functionality
new_findings.explanation: The system should include built-in health monitoring features that provide status updates regarding system performance, uptime, and any flagged issues. This ensures proactive management and quick responses to potential problems.

new_findings.name: Communication of system updates
new_findings.explanation: There should be a structured means to communicate updates or outages to users effectively. This could include a notification system that alerts staff of updates and any expected downtime as well as major changes to reporting functionality.

new_findings.name: Configurable user preference settings
new_findings.explanation: The system must offer user-configurable settings that allow staff to define their preferences for report formatting, visibility options, and notification settings, to improve usability and user satisfaction.

new_findings.name: Accessibility compliance update
new_findings.explanation: The requirements specify compliance with Section 508 and older browsers without confirmation on whether these legacy versions remain required or if the policy will be updated.

new_findings.name: Operational separation from OPAC
new_findings.explanation: The reporting system should not affect the performance of the OPAC module to prevent slowdowns for library patrons.

new_findings.name: Help system accessibility and navigation
new_findings.explanation: The online help system should be hierarchical, cross-linked, searchable, and easy to navigate to facilitate staff training and support.

new_findings.name: Reports interface specification adaptation
new_findings.explanation: The project intends to adapt an existing Software Requirements Specification (SRS) developed by Galecia Group for specific PINES needs, suggesting additional insights are required on adaptation processes.

new_findings.name: Functional requirements for reports and management processes
new_findings.explanation: The system must efficiently support reporting and analysis functions used by library managers, administrators, and staff for planning, evaluation, and oversight. These functions are explicitly scoped to management processes and do not include patron-facing OPAC or circulation functions.

new_findings.name: Report development and testing responsibilities
new_findings.explanation: The Reports Working Group is tasked with documenting optimal Reports functionality within a future Evergreen release, developing a list of requirements, and becoming the designated testing group to evaluate all new Reports development.
